title: Game Boy Color IPS Screen Mod: Worth It?
creator: Solder & Pixels
description:
Putting an IPS backlit screen into a 1999 Game Boy Color. Shell trimming, ribbon cable, brightness wire.

Torqit Mini driver kit: 10% off with code OWEN10 at https://torqit.gg/owen

Kit and parts list in the pinned comment.

sentences.t: Alright, the shell is closed, the screws are in, and it's the moment of truth.
I'm putting in two double A batteries, and if this doesn't turn on, I'm going to need a minute.
Okay, power switch.
There it is!
Look at that, look at how bright that is compared to the original screen I showed you at the start.
This is a Game Boy Color from 1999, and the original screen was completely unreadable unless you were sitting under a lamp, and now it looks like it came out of a phone.
Let's go back over the trickiest parts, because I know a lot of you are going to try this.
The hardest bit by far was trimming the shell.
This IPS kit is slightly thicker than the original panel, so you have to shave down two little plastic ribs inside the front half of the shell.
Go slowly, use a flush cutter, and test fit it about ten times, because you cannot un-cut plastic.
Second tricky part, the ribbon cable.
It's tiny, it's fragile, and it has to go in at exactly the right angle, so flip the latch up, slide it in, and close the latch without pulling on the cable.
I tore my first one doing this, which is why there's a cut in the video where I suddenly have a second kit.
Third, the brightness wire.
This kit lets you change brightness with a button combo, but you have to solder one thin wire from the screen board to the select button pad.
If soldering scares you, there are kits that skip this step, you just lose the brightness control.
If you're getting into this hobby, the one tool you don't want to cheap out on is your driver set, and the one I keep reaching for is the Torqit Mini.
It comes with sixty-four magnetic bits, including the tri-wing and gamebit ones that Nintendo loves, so you're never hunting for some weird screwdriver again.
The handle is aluminum, it spins on a little bearing at the top, and the case snaps shut magnetically so the bits don't end up all over your desk.
Every bit is covered by a lifetime warranty, which honestly is rare for anything at this price.
You can pick one up at torqit.gg slash owen, and if you use code OWEN10 at checkout you'll get ten percent off.
So, was it worth it?
The kit was about forty dollars, the console was sixty on a resale site, and the time was about two hours, not counting the ribbon cable incident.
For a Game Boy that I'll actually play now instead of keeping it in a drawer, yeah, absolutely worth it.
Let's put in Pokemon Crystal and see how the colors look.
Oh, that's gorgeous.
The greens are actually green.
Next week, I'm going to try putting a rechargeable battery in this thing, with USB-C charging, which involves cutting the battery compartment, so, pray for me.
If you have a handheld you want to see modded, leave it in the comments.
See you next time.
